paths.title: Create an order (POST create-order → OrderService.create → OrdersRepo.insert)
paths.rationale: Highest business impact times highest fragility. This is the only flow in which money is recorded, and every fragility signal in the repository converges on it: src/repo/orders_repo.py is the top hotspot (6 of 12 commits, one author, bus factor 1 across all of src/); the INSERT is retried without an idempotency key and already produced duplicate orders in production, fixed by reverting the attempt count from 3 to 2 rather than adding a key; the schema has no unique guard; the only authorization check compares two caller-supplied values (X-User header vs body user_id); the handler validates nothing (KeyError on a missing field, IntegrityError/DataError propagate unmapped); line items are summed and discarded; each request opens a psycopg2 connection that is never closed; and no test imports any of it, so CI stays green through a repeat of the incident. Entry confirmed by reading handle_create_order at L6-L11, which calls require_user (authz.py L8-L10), then OrderService.create (orders.py L9-L11), then OrdersRepo.insert (orders_repo.py L11-L25).
paths.businessImpact: Every sale enters the database through this path, and a duplicated, lost or misattributed insert is a direct revenue and customer-trust error that nothing in the system logs, guards or tests.

paths.title: Read an order by id (GET get-order → OrderService.get → OrdersRepo.fetch)
paths.rationale: Second because it is the other half of the entire HTTP surface and its fragility is a confirmed security hole rather than a latent one: handle_get_order (L14-L16) has never called require_user and is byte-identical to the initial import, order ids are a SERIAL sequence, and OrdersRepo.fetch (orders_repo.py L27-L31) selects by id alone, so every order's user_id and total is enumerable by any caller with no credentials. Ranked below creation because it does not write money, but each GET also opens a connection that is never closed and left idle in transaction, returns a Decimal total that stdlib json cannot serialize (while create returns a float), and raises TypeError for an unknown id because there is no not-found path. Zero test coverage, no logging, and identical bus-factor-1 ownership.
paths.businessImpact: Any client can read any customer's order (user id and amount) without authentication, a data-exposure incident that also degrades the database under ordinary read load.

paths.title: Deploy code to an environment (deploy/deploy.sh <env>)
paths.rationale: The deploy is the only route from a commit to production and it is a six-line, single-author script untouched since the initial import: it scp's the operator's local working tree of src/ (not a git ref, so uncommitted edits ship and nothing records the deployed revision), then hard-restarts a single systemd unit over ssh with no health check, drain or second instance. There is no rollback beyond redeploying the previous commit, CI never invokes it (so code can reach production having never passed or even been pushed through CI), the environment argument is an unconstrained hostname prefix with no confirmation, and requirements.txt, config/, templates/ and db/ are never shipped. Ranked below the two request paths because it runs on human demand rather than per customer, but a bad deploy takes down the whole environment with no trace of what was shipped.
paths.businessImpact: A mistyped environment name or an uncommitted local edit reaches production with downtime on every deploy, no rollback, and no record of which revision is running.

paths.title: Apply a schema migration by hand (db/migrations/ → psql → schema.sql)
paths.rationale: Schema changes are the second way production data is changed and they travel through a channel unrelated to the code deploy: raw SQL applied by hand with no migration runner, tracking table, transaction wrapper, down script or backup, and a single repository-wide '-- applied' comment that cannot say which environment has received which migration. Migration 002 is written, marked not applied, and drops users.address in the same script that creates addresses without copying any data, so applying it as written destroys every stored postal address irreversibly; the TODO blocking it cites a src/service dependency that never existed at any commit. Ranked fourth because it runs rarely and today's code touches no pending column, but the only person who has written migrations (bus factor 1 in db/) has never committed to src/, and the implicit three-step convention (run SQL, append to schema.sql, flip header) is documented nowhere.
paths.businessImpact: Applying or mis-ordering a hand-run migration can irreversibly destroy customer address data, with no rollback, backup or per-environment record anywhere in the repository.

untraced.title: CI smoke test (.github/workflows/ci.yml → tests/test_orders.sh)
untraced.reason: Not a flow the business depends on: the workflow runs a hermetic arithmetic assert that imports no project module, protects no branch, produces no artifact and is never consumed by deploy.sh, so it gates nothing. Its facts (F-map-ci-*, F-lens-security-tests-010) are cited from the production-deploy and order-creation paths instead of traced separately.

untraced.title: Send order-confirmation email (templates/email.tmpl)
untraced.reason: No entry point exists at HEAD: nothing renders or sends the template, no template engine or mail client is declared, and the context it needs (user.name) has no backing column. It is an unwired asset (F-map-ops-019, F-lens-deploy-ops-019, F-lens-landmines-glossary-006), so there is no code path to follow hop by hop.

untraced.title: List a user's orders (OrdersRepo.list_for_user)
untraced.reason: Unreachable from the HTTP surface: no handler or service calls list_for_user (F-map-src-032), so despite its N+1 hotfix history and missing index (F-map-db-008) there is no entry point to trace. Anyone exposing it must add require_user themselves (F-lens-landmines-glossary-011).

untraced.title: User sign-up, login or user record creation
untraced.reason: No such flow exists in the repository: nothing inserts into users, there is no authentication, and identity is a plain X-User header (F-map-src-013, F-lens-data-migrations-003). The only identity-related code, require_user, is traced as the authorization hop of order-creation.

untraced.title: gRPC client (vendor/generated/client_pb2.py)
untraced.reason: Generated code imported by nothing, with no .proto source, protoc step or protobuf runtime in the repository (F-lens-deploy-ops-020, F-lens-landmines-glossary-007). vendor/ is inventoried only and must not be mapped or traced.

untraced.title: Bootstrap a fresh 'orders' database (create DB, load schema.sql, seed users)
untraced.reason: A developer setup procedure rather than a business flow, and entirely unscripted: the README omits it, schema.sql plus the migrations folder conflict on 001, and no users seed exists so the first order fails on the FK (F-map-db-010, F-map-db-017, F-map-ops-026, F-lens-landmines-glossary-010). Its landmines are cited from the schema-migration and order-creation paths.
